name: Otomanguean Family

linguisticChallenges.tonalComplexity: Otomanguean languages are tonal, many with complex tonal systems (Mixtec varieties have up to 8+ tone levels/contours). Tone often carries both lexical and grammatical information. Orthographic representation of tone varies across communities and is often incomplete.
linguisticChallenges.headInitial: Most Otomanguean languages are head-initial (VSO or VOS word order), which differs from the SOV or SVO patterns more familiar to MT systems.

notes: Minimal family card for Otomanguean (~180 members). A major Mesoamerican language family including Zapotec, Mixtec, Otomi, Mazatec, Chinantec, and others. All spoken in Mexico. Tonal systems and head-initial word order are the most consistently shared features. Many members are endangered.

regions.region: Oaxaca, Puebla, Guerrero, State of Mexico, Hidalgo, and surrounding states
